description: Blocks in the Simulink > Sources library, which have outputs but no inputs and therefore supply the stimuli that drive a model: constants, analytic waveforms, random and noise generators, simulation time, and readers that stream recorded data in from the MATLAB workspace, a MAT-file or a spreadsheet. Every parameter listed here is the programmatic name accepted by set_param and by add_block name-value arguments.

tools.name: Constant
tools.description: Outputs a value that never changes during the simulation. The value may be a scalar, vector, matrix or N-D array and can be any MATLAB expression, so it is the usual way to feed a tunable workspace variable or a calibration coefficient into a diagram. Its default sample time of inf marks the output as constant, which lets Simulink optimise everything downstream of it.
tools.usage: Simulink > Sources > Constant (also Simulink > Commonly Used Blocks)

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: Constant output. Any expression evaluating to a scalar, vector, matrix or N-D array; typically a workspace variable name for tunability.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Output sample time. Default 'inf' means the output is genuinely constant; set a finite value to force periodic output.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output data type, e.g. 'Inherit: Inherit from Constant value', 'double', 'int32', 'fixdt(1,16,0)', 'Enum: MyEnum'.

parameters.name: VectorParams1D
parameters.description: 'on' (default) treats a vector Value as a 1-D signal; 'off' keeps it as a row or column matrix.

parameters.name: OutMin / OutMax
parameters.description: Design range used for range checking and for fixed-point autoscaling.

tools.notes: Setting Value to a workspace variable keeps the block tunable, which matters for code generation and for Simulink.SimulationInput sweeps. Use Enumerated Constant when the output must be an enumeration member.

tools.name: Step
tools.description: Generates a step: the output holds the initial value until the step time, then jumps to the final value and stays there. It is the standard stimulus for measuring the transient response, rise time and overshoot of a control loop or filter. Zero-crossing detection is on by default so a variable-step solver lands exactly on the discontinuity.

parameters.name: Time
parameters.description: Step time in seconds at which the output changes. Default '1'.

parameters.name: InitialValue
parameters.description: Output before the step time. Default '0'.

parameters.name: FinalValue
parameters.description: Output at and after the step time. Default '1'.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Sample time; '0' (default) gives a continuous output, a positive value a discrete one.

parameters.name: ZeroCross
parameters.description: 'on' (default) enables zero-crossing detection so the solver does not step over the transition.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output data type: 'double' (default), 'single', 'Inherit: Inherit via back propagation' or a data type expression.

tools.notes: For a negative-going step simply set InitialValue above FinalValue. For a pulse rather than a step use Pulse Generator; for a step at t=0 set Time to '0', which also avoids an unnecessary solver reset.

tools.name: Ramp
tools.description: Generates a signal that increases (or decreases) linearly with time after a start time, holding an initial output before it. Use it to sweep an input slowly through a range to trace a static characteristic, to test rate limiters and slew-rate constraints, or as a simple time base. The slope may be negative for a falling ramp.

parameters.name: slope
parameters.description: Rate of change of the output per second. Default '1'; negative values ramp downwards.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Time in seconds at which the ramp begins. Default '0'.

parameters.name: InitialOutput
parameters.description: Output value held before the start time. Default '0'.

parameters.name: VectorParams1D
parameters.description: 'on' (default) interprets vector parameters as 1-D signals.

tools.notes: Note the lower-case programmatic names 'slope' and 'start' — the dialog labels are Slope and Start time. A ramp is unbounded, so clamp it with a Saturation block when driving a plant that must stay in range.

tools.name: Sine Wave
tools.description: Generates a sinusoid with configurable amplitude, bias, frequency and phase. In the default time-based mode it evaluates the sine from simulation time, which is exact but can drift over very long runs; sample-based mode instead steps a discrete recurrence defined by samples per period, which is better for long discrete simulations and for code generation. Frequency is specified in radians per second, not hertz.

parameters.name: SineType
parameters.description: 'Time based' (default) computes from simulation time; 'Sample based' uses a discrete recurrence with Samples per period.

parameters.name: Amplitude
parameters.description: Peak amplitude of the sinusoid. Default '1'.

parameters.name: Bias
parameters.description: Constant added to the sinusoid. Default '0'.

parameters.name: Frequency
parameters.description: Angular frequency in rad/s (time-based mode only). Enter 2*pi*f for f hertz.

parameters.name: Phase
parameters.description: Phase offset in radians (time-based mode only).

parameters.name: Samples
parameters.description: Samples per period (sample-based mode only).

parameters.name: Offset
parameters.description: Number of offset samples, i.e. the phase shift in samples (sample-based mode only).

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Sample time. '0' gives a continuous signal in time-based mode; must be positive in sample-based mode.

parameters.name: TimeSource
parameters.description: 'Use simulation time' (default) or 'Use external signal', which adds an input port for the time value.

tools.notes: Time-based mode with a continuous sample time accumulates rounding error in very long runs; switch to sample-based mode for those. Signal Generator and Waveform Generator provide square, sawtooth and multi-segment waveforms from the same library.

tools.name: Pulse Generator
tools.description: Produces a rectangular pulse train defined by amplitude, period, duty cycle and phase delay. Time-based mode computes edges from simulation time and works with variable-step solvers; sample-based mode counts solver steps and is preferred for discrete models and code generation. It is the usual source for PWM drive signals, clock enables and periodic triggers.

parameters.name: PulseType
parameters.description: 'Time based' (default) or 'Sample based'. Sample-based mode counts samples instead of using simulation time.

parameters.name: Amplitude
parameters.description: Height of the pulse. Default '1'.

parameters.name: Period
parameters.description: Pulse period in seconds (time-based) or in number of samples (sample-based). Default '10'.

parameters.name: PulseWidth
parameters.description: Duty cycle as a percentage of the period, 0 to 100 (time-based), or a number of samples (sample-based). Default '5'.

parameters.name: PhaseDelay
parameters.description: Delay in seconds (or samples) before the first pulse. Default '0'.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Sample time. Default '1'. In sample-based mode it must be positive and finite.

parameters.name: TimeSource
parameters.description: 'Use simulation time' (default) or 'Use external signal' to drive the time base from an input port.

tools.notes: With a fixed-step solver in time-based mode, make the period, phase delay and pulse width exact integer multiples of the step size or edges will be quantised. A PulseWidth that makes the on-time zero or equal to the whole period is rejected in time-based mode.

tools.name: Signal Generator
tools.description: A compact four-in-one waveform source producing a sine, square, sawtooth or uniformly distributed random signal from a single amplitude and frequency setting. Unlike Sine Wave it can express frequency directly in hertz, and unlike Pulse Generator its square wave is symmetric and bipolar. Use it for quick stimulus during model bring-up when you want to switch waveform shape from one dialog field.

parameters.name: WaveForm
parameters.description: 'sine' (default), 'square', 'sawtooth' or 'random'.

parameters.name: Amplitude
parameters.description: Peak amplitude of the generated waveform. Default '1'.

parameters.name: Frequency
parameters.description: Frequency of the waveform, interpreted in the chosen Units. Default '1'.

parameters.name: Units
parameters.description: 'rad/sec' (default) or 'Hertz' — which unit the Frequency parameter is expressed in.

parameters.name: TimeSource
parameters.description: 'Use simulation time' (default) or 'Use external signal' to supply the time base through an input port.

parameters.name: VectorParams1D
parameters.description: 'on' (default) interprets vector amplitude and frequency as 1-D signals.

tools.notes: The block always outputs double precision and has no data-type parameter. For controllable duty cycle use Pulse Generator; for arbitrary multi-segment waveforms use Waveform Generator.

tools.name: Chirp Signal
tools.description: Generates a sine wave whose frequency rises linearly from an initial frequency to a target frequency over a specified target time, then continues sweeping in the same linear fashion. A swept sine is the standard excitation for measuring the frequency response of a nonlinear or time-varying system, where a single-frequency sine would tell you nothing about the rest of the band. All three parameters are in hertz and seconds.

parameters.name: f1
parameters.description: Initial frequency in hertz at t = 0. Default '0.1'.

parameters.name: T
parameters.description: Target time in seconds at which the frequency reaches f2. Default '100'.

parameters.name: f2
parameters.description: Frequency in hertz reached at the target time. Default '1'.

parameters.name: VectorParams1D
parameters.description: 'on' (default) interprets vector parameters as 1-D signals, allowing several chirps from one block.

tools.notes: The sweep does not stop at the target time — the frequency keeps increasing at the same rate, so set the model StopTime to T if you only want the specified band. Amplitude is fixed at 1; scale it with a Gain block.

tools.name: Waveform Generator
tools.description: Outputs arbitrary waveforms built from a signal-notation string that chains functions such as sin, square, sawtooth, pulse, gaussnoise, step and constant, including repeats and sequences. One block can hold several named waveform definitions and switch between them with the Selected signal parameter, which makes it a compact replacement for a stack of separate source blocks. Unlike the older sources it exposes full output data type, rounding and saturation control.

parameters.name: SelectedSignal
parameters.description: Which of the defined waveform rows the block currently outputs.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Interval between output samples. Default '0' for continuous.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output data type, including fixed-point types.

parameters.name: OutMin / OutMax
parameters.description: Design range used for range checking and fixed-point autoscaling.

parameters.name: RndMeth
parameters.description: Rounding mode applied to fixed-point results: 'Floor', 'Nearest', 'Round', 'Zero', 'Ceiling', 'Simplest', 'Convergent'.

parameters.name: SaturateOnIntegerOverflow
parameters.description: 'on' saturates on integer overflow, 'off' wraps.

parameters.name: LockScale
parameters.description: 'on' prevents the Fixed-Point Tool from overriding the specified data type.

tools.notes: The waveform definitions themselves are edited in the block dialog table; the programmatic parameters above control which one is active and how it is typed. Use it when a test stimulus is a sequence of segments that would otherwise need several sources plus switching logic.

tools.name: Random Number
tools.description: Generates normally distributed (Gaussian) random numbers with a specified mean and variance, producing a new value at every sample time. The sequence is repeatable for a given seed, so simulations stay reproducible across runs and machines. Use it for measurement noise, process disturbance and Monte Carlo studies in discrete models.

parameters.name: Mean
parameters.description: Mean of the normal distribution. Default '0'.

parameters.name: Variance
parameters.description: Variance of the distribution. Default '1' (standard deviation 1).

parameters.name: Seed
parameters.description: Starting seed of the generator. Default '0'. Identical seeds give identical sequences.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Interval at which a new random value is produced. Default '0.1'.

parameters.name: VectorParams1D
parameters.description: 'on' (default); with vector Mean/Variance/Seed the block outputs a vector of independent streams.

tools.notes: Because the output is piecewise constant between sample times, this block is inappropriate as continuous noise into a variable-step solver — use Band-Limited White Noise there instead. Give each noise source a different seed, otherwise supposedly independent channels will be perfectly correlated.

tools.name: Uniform Random Number
tools.description: Generates random numbers drawn uniformly from the interval between a minimum and a maximum, one new value per sample time. Uniform noise is the right model for quantisation error, dither and random parameter draws where every value in a range is equally likely. As with Random Number, a fixed seed makes the sequence repeatable.

parameters.name: Minimum
parameters.description: Lower bound of the interval. Default '-1'.

parameters.name: Maximum
parameters.description: Upper bound of the interval. Default '1'.

parameters.name: Seed
parameters.description: Starting seed; must be 0 or a positive integer. Default '0'.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Interval at which a new value is drawn. Default '0.1'.

parameters.name: VectorParams1D
parameters.description: 'on' (default) interprets vector parameters as 1-D signals for independent channels.

tools.notes: All the numeric parameters must have the same dimensions after scalar expansion. To build a Gaussian stream instead, use Random Number; to make a normal stream suitable for continuous systems, use Band-Limited White Noise.

tools.name: Band-Limited White Noise
tools.description: Introduces normally distributed noise with an approximately flat spectrum up to a bandwidth set by its sample time, correctly scaled so that the noise power matches the specified value in a continuous simulation. True white noise has infinite power, so a continuous model needs this band-limited approximation rather than a plain random source. It is the standard disturbance and sensor-noise source for Kalman filter and control robustness studies.

parameters.name: Cov
parameters.description: Noise power — the height of the power spectral density of the white noise. Default '[0.1]'.

parameters.name: Ts
parameters.description: Sample time, which sets the noise correlation time and hence the bandwidth. Default '0.1'.

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: Starting seed of the generator. Default '[23341]'.

parameters.name: VectorParams1D
parameters.description: 'on' (default) interprets vector parameters as 1-D signals, giving independent noise channels.

tools.notes: Note the unusual lower-case parameter names Ts and seed. Set Ts to roughly one hundredth of the smallest time constant of interest so the noise looks white over the system's bandwidth. The output is always double precision.

tools.name: Repeating Sequence
tools.description: Outputs an arbitrary periodic waveform defined by a pair of vectors: a strictly increasing vector of times within one period and a matching vector of output values. Simulink interpolates linearly between the specified points and repeats the pattern forever, with the period equal to the span of the time vector. Use it for drive cycles, custom triangular or trapezoidal waveforms, and any repeating profile that no analytic source block produces.

parameters.name: rep_seq_t
parameters.description: Time values within one period — a strictly monotonically increasing vector. Default '[0 2]'.

parameters.name: rep_seq_y
parameters.description: Output values at the corresponding times. Default '[0 2]'.

tools.notes: The two vectors must be the same length. For the output to be continuous across the period boundary the first and last output values should match. Repeating Sequence Stair holds each value instead of interpolating, and Repeating Sequence Interpolated gives control over the interpolation method and sample time.

tools.name: Repeating Sequence Stair
tools.description: Outputs the elements of a vector one per sample time, holding each value until the next, and repeats the sequence indefinitely. Because it is purely discrete and holds rather than interpolates, it is the right choice for scripted test patterns, gear or mode sequences, and lookup-style stimulus in fixed-step and code-generation models. It exposes full output data type control including fixed-point.

parameters.name: OutValues
parameters.description: Vector of output values emitted one per sample time before the sequence repeats. Default '[3 1 4 2 1].'''.

parameters.name: tsamp
parameters.description: Sample time — how long each element is held. Default '-1' (inherited).

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output data type: 'double' (default), 'single', integer types, 'Inherit: Inherit via back propagation' or a data type expression.

parameters.name: OutMin / OutMax
parameters.description: Design range used for range checking and fixed-point autoscaling.

parameters.name: LockScale
parameters.description: 'on' prevents the Fixed-Point Tool from overriding the output data type.

tools.notes: The sample-time parameter is named tsamp, not SampleTime. Because there is no interpolation, the output is piecewise constant and has discontinuities at every sample instant — fine for discrete models, less suitable as a continuous plant input.

tools.name: Clock
tools.description: Outputs the current simulation time at every solver step as a continuous double signal. Use it wherever a computation depends explicitly on time — gain scheduling, time-varying references, or logging a time stamp alongside data. The block can optionally show the running time on its icon, which is handy while watching a long simulation.

parameters.name: DisplayTime
parameters.description: 'off' (default) or 'on' — show the current simulation time on the block icon.

parameters.name: Decimation
parameters.description: Positive integer controlling how often the icon display updates, in solver steps. Default '10'. Only relevant when DisplayTime is 'on'.

tools.notes: For a discrete model use Digital Clock instead, since the continuous Clock output changes at every minor step and forces the block downstream to be continuous. For code generation, a Clock feeding into a discrete subsystem is usually a sign that Digital Clock was the right block.

tools.name: Digital Clock
tools.description: Outputs the simulation time, but only updates it at a specified sampling interval, holding the value in between. This makes the time signal genuinely discrete, which is what a discrete controller, a data logger or generated code expects. Use it in place of the continuous Clock block anywhere the consuming subsystem runs at a fixed rate.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Interval at which the output is updated, in seconds. Default '1'. May also be a 1-by-2 vector [period offset] with 0 <= offset < period.

tools.notes: Do not give this source a continuous sample time (0 or [0 0]) or an inherited one (-1): as a source block it has nothing to inherit from, and both cases are errors or produce a meaningless result. Period and offset must be finite and non-negative.

tools.name: From Workspace
tools.description: Streams recorded data from a MATLAB workspace variable into the model as a signal. It accepts timeseries and timetable objects, structures with time, and plain [time, data] matrices, and interpolates between samples when the solver asks for a time between data points. Use it to replay measured data, to feed a plant model with a recorded input, or to close a loop around data captured from an earlier run.

parameters.name: VariableName
parameters.description: The workspace expression supplying the data: a variable name, timeseries, timetable, structure with time, or a 2-D [t data] matrix.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Output sample time. Default '0' (continuous); a positive value resamples the data onto a discrete rate.

parameters.name: Interpolate
parameters.description: 'on' (default) linearly interpolates between data points; 'off' holds the previous value.

parameters.name: OutputAfterFinalValue
parameters.description: Behaviour past the last data point: 'Extrapolation', 'Setting to zero', 'Holding final value' or 'Cyclic repetition'.

parameters.name: ZeroCross
parameters.description: 'on' (default) enables zero-crossing detection at data discontinuities.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output data type, e.g. 'Inherit: auto', 'double', 'int32', 'Bus: myBus', 'Enum: myEnum'.

tools.notes: The variable is resolved in the model workspace first, then the base workspace, at the start of simulation — a Simulink.SimulationInput setVariable call is the clean way to supply it per run. For data too large to hold in memory use From File (MAT-file, streamed) or From Spreadsheet. To drive root-level Inport blocks instead, use setExternalInput on a SimulationInput object.

tools.name: From File
tools.description: Reads time-stamped data incrementally from a MAT-file and outputs it as a signal, loading only the samples it needs rather than the whole file. That makes it the right choice for long recordings and large logged data sets that would not fit comfortably in the MATLAB workspace. You control how it behaves before the first sample, between samples and after the last sample independently.

parameters.name: FileName
parameters.description: Name or path of the MAT-file holding the data. Default 'untitled.mat'.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Output sample time. Default '0' for continuous; a positive value or [period offset] for discrete output.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output data type: 'Inherit (auto)' (default), a built-in type, a fixed-point type, 'Enum: <class>' or 'Bus: <object>'.

parameters.name: ExtrapolationBeforeFirstDataPoint
parameters.description: 'Linear extrapolation' (default), 'Hold first value' or 'Ground value'.

parameters.name: InterpolationWithinTimeRange
parameters.description: 'Linear interpolation' (default) or 'Zero order hold'.

parameters.name: ExtrapolationAfterLastDataPoint
parameters.description: 'Linear extrapolation' (default), 'Hold last value' or 'Ground value'.

parameters.name: ZeroCross
parameters.description: 'on' (default) enables zero-crossing detection at data discontinuities.

tools.notes: The MAT-file must contain time-stamped data (a timeseries, a Dataset element, or a matrix whose first row or column is time) — an arbitrary variable will not load. Files written by the To File block or by the Record block are directly readable. Linear extrapolation past the end of the data can produce wildly wrong values, so 'Hold last value' is usually safer.

tools.name: From Spreadsheet
tools.description: Reads time-stamped signal data from a Microsoft Excel workbook or a CSV file and streams it into the model, one sheet and cell range at a time. It removes the intermediate step of importing test data into MATLAB first, which matters when the source of truth is a lab spreadsheet that changes often. Interpolation and extrapolation behaviour before, within and after the data range are all configurable.

parameters.name: FileName
parameters.description: Full or relative path of the .xlsx, .xls or .csv file, including the extension.

parameters.name: SheetName
parameters.description: Name of the worksheet to read.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: Cell range to read, e.g. 'A1:B3,D1:D3'. Empty reads the used range of the sheet.

parameters.name: TreatFirstColumnAs
parameters.description: 'Time' (the first column holds time stamps) or 'Data'.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Output sample time; use a positive value to resample onto a discrete rate.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output data type for the signal read from the sheet.

parameters.name: InterpolationWithinTimeRange
parameters.description: 'Linear interpolation' or 'Zero order hold'.

parameters.name: ExtrapolationBeforeFirstDataPoint / ExtrapolationAfterLastDataPoint
parameters.description: 'Linear extrapolation', 'Hold first/last value' or 'Ground value'.

parameters.name: OutputAfterLastPoint
parameters.description: 'Repeating sequence', 'Hold final value' or 'Ground value'.

tools.notes: On Windows the block reads Excel files through COM by default (ReaderLibrary 'COM'), which requires Excel to be installed; set ReaderLibrary to 'LibXL' to read without Excel. Time values must be monotonically increasing. CSV files are supported directly.

tools.name: Signal Editor
tools.description: Holds a library of interchangeable test scenarios inside a single block and outputs the signals of whichever scenario is active, with one output port per signal. The Signal Editor user interface lets you draw, import and edit those signals graphically and store them all in one MAT-file. It is the standard way to manage a suite of test cases for a model without swapping source blocks or juggling workspace variables.

parameters.name: Filename
parameters.description: MAT-file holding the scenarios and their signal data. Default 'untitled.mat'.

parameters.name: ActiveScenario
parameters.description: Name or numeric index of the scenario to output. Change it to switch test cases between runs.

parameters.name: ActiveSignal
parameters.description: Name or index of the signal within the scenario whose properties the dialog is editing.

parameters.name: SignalPropertySource
parameters.description: 'Dialog parameters' or 'Signal data in MAT file' — where signal attributes come from.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Output sample time; '-1' inherits, or give the sample period in seconds.

parameters.name: Interpolate
parameters.description: 'on' interpolates between the stored data points, 'off' holds.

parameters.name: OutputAfterFinalValue
parameters.description: 'Setting to zero', 'Extrapolation' or 'Holding final value' past the end of the scenario.

parameters.name: IsBus
parameters.description: 'on' when the scenario's signals form a bus.

tools.notes: Sweeping ActiveScenario with Simulink.SimulationInput setBlockParameter is the idiomatic way to run a whole test suite from a script. The signalEditor function opens the editing user interface on a MAT-file directly from MATLAB.

tools.name: Ground
tools.description: Supplies a zero-valued signal of whatever data type the port it feeds expects, so that an input port which genuinely has nothing connected does not produce an unconnected-port warning. It adapts automatically to double, integer, fixed-point, boolean, enumerated and bus types. Use it to cap unused inputs on library blocks and on subsystems where only some ports are meaningful in a given configuration.
tools.usage: Simulink > Sources > Ground (also Simulink > Commonly Used Blocks)
tools.notes: For a fixed-point type with a bias that cannot represent zero exactly, the block outputs the closest representable value instead of exactly zero; for an enumerated type it outputs the default member, or the first one declared if there is no default. Terminator is the mirror-image block for unconnected output ports.
